known.title: Run a full review after replaying a stacked part
Resolve the actual default branch in the PR-check checkout

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - closing a previously reviewed child after its base merges.
The replay forces `fresh` false, but this call still passes the pre-replay `previous` review. `review.instructions()` at src/forge/review.py:380-382 consequently appends the repair-review instructions from src/forge/templates/review.md:481-488, which prohibit a fresh review and allow only new P0 findings. The new invocation therefore cannot report ordinary P1 defects exposed by integrating the child with merged code. Request a full review after replay while retaining historical findings separately. The named tests count review invocations but do not check this restriction.
findings.title: Run a full review after replaying a stacked part

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client repository whose default branch is `master` runs the generated GitHub check.
The generated workflow checks out the base SHA (src/forge/prcheck.py:140-153). [actions/checkout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/checkout/v7/src/git-source-provider.ts) initializes a repository and fetches explicit refspecs; it does not establish `origin/HEAD`. [Git's fetch implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.51.0/builtin/fetch.c) also skips creating that symbolic ref for explicit refspecs. Consequently `repo.default_branch()` falls back to `main` (src/forge/repo.py:440-444). This guard then looks for the merged parent on nonexistent `origin/main` and permanently refuses the child, even after its parent merged and close replayed it onto `master`. Resolve the default branch from trusted CI metadata or establish its remote symbolic ref before checking it.
findings.title: Resolve the actual default branch in the PR-check checkout
